result.summary: Clear pending buffer bytes before invoking the underlying stream write in `BufferedWriter::flush()` to avoid re-attempting writes during exception unwinding. Explicitly call `flush()` within try-catch blocks in `BlockManager::WriteBlock` and `BlockManager::WriteBlockUndo` so disk write errors trigger clean fatal error handling instead of aborting the process.
result.problem: When block or undo writes fail due to disk issues (such as a full filesystem), `AutoFile::write_buffer()` throws an exception. Because `BufferedWriter` previously flushed pending bytes in its implicitly `noexcept` destructor, write failures invoked `std::terminate` instead of normal node storage error handling, and a failed explicit `flush()` would re-attempt the write upon destructor unwinding.
evidence: Author report: 'my 1 TB benchmarking servers have recently been filling up, so I've been seeing these failures more often.'
PR description provides a minimal reproduction script demonstrating that short writes previously resulted in process aborts rather than a clean exit with 'Failed to write genesis block'.
The bug was introduced in merged PR #31551, which added `BufferedWriter`.
result.changed_since_previous: No substantial changes to the code or approach; commits now credit a co-author and refine unit test coverage.
result.card: Prevents bitcoind from abruptly crashing via std::terminate when block or undo writes fail due to disk storage errors such as a full disk. BlockManager now explicitly flushes buffered writers within try-catch blocks to route errors to standard shutdown procedures, and BufferedWriter clears pending buffer offsets before writing to avoid re-triggering writes during stack unwinding. The author observed repeated crashes on 1 TB benchmark servers running out of space and provided a reproducer demonstrating that write failures now exit cleanly.

risk.why: A flaw in block and undo write flush handling could lead to silent data loss or premature fatal errors during block storage.
